% sections/appendix.tex -- full result tables (all generated by
% experiments/aggregate.py). Typeset in the text flow (not as floats) and
% ordered so that each full latency table shares a page with a small table.
\section{Full result tables}\label{sec:appendix}

The tables below list every instance and method of E1--E8. Latencies are per
update in \textmu s, the updates of the three runs pooled. A $'$ marks
\method{gudhi} on the prefix $T'={}$\NumPrefix{}; an empty cell means that the
method is not part of that experiment.

\newcommand{\appendixtable}[3]{% #1 label, #2 caption, #3 generated file stem
  \par\bigskip
  \begin{minipage}{\linewidth}
    \centering
    \captionsetup{hypcap=false}%
    \captionof{table}{#2}\label{#1}
    \scriptsize
    \setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
    \generatedtable{#3}
  \end{minipage}\par}

\appendixtable{tab:w4-betti}{W4: ranges of the Betti numbers over all states of
  the three runs, and $\beta_D/n$ at INIT. $\beta_D$ is dominated by unfilled
  boundaries of $(D+2)$-cliques (\cref{sec:exp-workloads}).}{tab_w4_betti}

\appendixtable{tab:full-amort}{Amortised per-update latency (\textmu s) of every
  instance of E1--E6. The \method{mmhm-norb} entry for W2 with $N=22$, $s=8$ (in
  E1 and E2) is inflated by one slow run with the same column additions as
  \method{mmhm} (\cref{sec:e1}).}{tab_summary_full}

\appendixtable{tab:rebuild-effect}{Does a rebuild help? Instances on which the
  default policy ($\alpha=1$, no period) rebuilt: amortised latency (\textmu s) of
  the four DRB methods, rebuilds per run, and the column additions of the
  rebuilding method in the 100 updates after each of its rebuilds divided by
  those of its never-rebuilding twin on the same updates (above~1: the rebuild
  made the following updates costlier).}{tab_rebuild_effect}

\appendixtable{tab:full-med}{Median per-update latency (\textmu s) of every
  instance of E1--E6.}{tab_summary_full_med}

\appendixtable{tab:e8}{What the Morse order buys (E8): median and p99 of the
  column additions and of the footprint ($\sum|\occ(\sigma)|$ over the deletions)
  per update, over the updates without a rebuild, and $\nnz(R)+\nnz(V)$ after
  INIT and at the end (means over the runs).}{tab_e8}

\appendixtable{tab:full-p99}{99th-percentile per-update latency (\textmu s) of
  every instance of E1--E6. The \method{mmhm-norb} entry for W2 with $N=22$,
  $s=8$ is inflated by one slow run (\cref{sec:e1}).}{tab_summary_full_p99}

\appendixtable{tab:e7}{Rebuild policy (E7): rebuilds per run (rb, mean over the
  runs), amortised and p99 per-update latency (\textmu s) of \method{mmhm} and
  \method{drb-id-rb} for each growth threshold $\alpha$ and period $m$. With
  $\alpha$ and the period off the methods never rebuild.}{tab_e7}
